title: The expression has an incompatible type
description: Elm infers a type for each expression and rejects an expression when it cannot unify that inferred type with the type required by its context. The compiler reports both sides of the mismatch so the unsafe conversion never reaches JavaScript output.

title: A proof obligation cannot be solved
description: Idris treats types as logical propositions. Applying Refl asserts two terms are definitionally equal, so the compiler rejects it when the required equality cannot be proven from the available terms.
bad_example:
onlyZero : (n : Nat) -> n = Z -> Nat
onlyZero n Refl = n
bad : Nat
bad = onlyZero (S Z) Refl
good_example:
onlyZero : (n : Nat) -> n = Z -> Nat
onlyZero n Refl = n
good : Nat
good = onlyZero Z Refl

title: A hole leaves an unsolved metavariable
description: Agda turns an omitted term into a metavariable and checks whether unification can determine it. A polymorphic function with no input evidence leaves that metavariable unsolved, so the module is rejected.
bad_example:
postulate A : Set
bad : A
bad = ?
good_example:
postulate A : Set
good : A -> A
good x = x

title: A value violates a function contract
description: Racket contracts wrap a boundary with predicates. Calling a value through a numeric contract with a string causes the wrapper to raise a contract violation before the implementation receives an invalid value.

title: An identifier has no binding in the active environment
description: Scheme evaluation resolves an identifier through the lexical and top-level environments. Referencing a name that was never defined leaves no value to evaluate and raises an unbound-variable condition.

title: An arithmetic operator received invalid operands
description: Erlang arithmetic BIFs require numeric operands and valid arithmetic operations. Dividing by zero raises the badarith reason, which propagates as a process exception unless caught.

code: No type class instance was found
title: A required type-class instance is unavailable
description: PureScript resolves constrained functions through type-class dictionaries at compile time. Asking show to render a function requires a Show instance for that function type, which the standard library deliberately does not provide.

title: An identifier is not declared in scope
description: Nim resolves names before it can type-check an expression. Using a name with no visible declaration prevents semantic analysis from determining what the expression refers to.

code: template does not match any template declaration
title: No template specialization satisfies the constraint
description: D selects a template specialization only when its type arguments and any constraint are satisfied. Passing string to a template constrained to int leaves no viable specialization.
bad_example:
template OnlyInt(T) if (is(T == int)) { alias OnlyInt = T; }
alias Value = OnlyInt!string;
good_example:
template OnlyInt(T) if (is(T == int)) { alias OnlyInt = T; }
alias Value = OnlyInt!int;

title: No method overload accepts the inferred argument types
description: Crystal performs static type inference and method overload selection before generating code. Adding a String to an Int32 has no matching overload, so compilation stops rather than inserting an implicit conversion.

title: An assignment crosses incompatible intrinsic types
description: Fortran requires assignments to obey the target variable's declared type and conversion rules. Assigning a character literal directly to an integer has no valid intrinsic assignment conversion.
bad_example:
program bad
  integer :: value
  value = "text"
end program bad
good_example:
program good
  integer :: value
  value = 42
end program good

title: A constrained subtype receives a value outside its range
description: Ada subtypes carry runtime constraints. When a range check detects that a value falls outside the declared bounds, the runtime raises Constraint_Error instead of silently storing an invalid value.

title: A numeric value exceeds its declared picture
description: COBOL PICTURE clauses define the size and decimal shape of a data item. Moving a value that needs more digits than the receiving picture can represent triggers implementation-specific size-error or truncation handling.

title: A moved value is used again
description: Cairo's ownership model tracks moves for values that cannot be implicitly copied. Assigning an owned array transfers it, so using the original binding afterward is rejected to preserve resource safety.

title: Checked arithmetic exceeds an unsigned integer range
description: Vyper arithmetic is checked. Adding one to the maximum uint8 value cannot be represented, so execution reverts with an overflow exception instead of wrapping as unchecked arithmetic would.

code: does not have the copy ability
title: A resource value is copied without the copy ability
description: Move distinguishes resource values from copyable values through abilities. A struct declared only with key is linear, so returning it from a function by value moves it; attempting an explicit copy is rejected by ability checking.

title: A loop start has no closing bracket
description: Brainfuck loops are paired by matching [ and ]. An interpreter or compiler cannot determine the jump target for an unmatched opening bracket, so it must reject the program before execution.

title: A flow-control instruction targets no declared label
description: Whitespace encodes labels and jumps with space, tab, and line-feed tokens. If a call or jump references a label never declared by a label instruction, the interpreter cannot choose the next instruction.
bad_example: # A jump instruction encoded for label 1, with no matching label declaration.
good_example: # Declare label 1 before encoding a jump or call to label 1.

title: An application expression is incomplete
description: Unlambda uses a backtick as a binary application operator, so it must be followed by two expressions. A source file ending immediately after a backtick leaves the parser without the required operands.

title: A function is called without a visible declaration
description: C compilation needs a visible declaration to type-check a call. Modern C modes reject an undeclared function instead of guessing its return type and calling convention.
good_example:
int total(void) { return 42; }
int main(void) { return total(); }

code: Element not allowed as child of p
title: A block element is nested inside a paragraph
description: HTML parsing closes a p element before block-level content such as div. Validators report the invalid tree because the source structure does not match the content model for p.

title: A property declaration is missing its colon
description: CSS declarations use a property-name colon value grammar. Without the colon, the parser cannot distinguish the property from its value and drops or reports the malformed declaration.

title: Nounset expansion references an unset variable
description: With set -u enabled, Bash treats expansion of an unset variable as an error. Initializing the value or supplying a default keeps automation scripts from continuing with an accidental empty value.

code: value of optional type must be unwrapped
title: An optional is used as though it were a concrete value
description: Swift represents a possibly absent value as Optional. Member access requires an explicit unwrap because the compiler cannot assume that the optional contains a value at this program point.
good_example:
let title: String? = "LexiconError"
if let title { print(title.count) }

title: A symbol does not resolve in the evaluation environment
description: R evaluates names by searching the current environment and its parents. Calling a function with an unbound object fails before the calculation can run.

title: A query references a relation that does not exist
description: A SQL engine resolves table names during statement preparation. Querying a table absent from the current schema fails rather than treating it as an empty relation.
good_example:
CREATE TABLE diagnostics (code TEXT);
SELECT * FROM diagnostics;

title: A name cannot be resolved in scope
description: Kotlin resolves local, imported, and member names before type checking. Referencing a missing symbol leaves no declaration to bind and produces an unresolved-reference diagnostic.
